key_insight: HairDeck treats a stylized hairstyle as an unordered set of hair cards rather than a long sequence of control points. This matches how artists construct card-based hair and targets animation-ready reconstruction from a single image.
problem_solved: Existing image-based approaches generate realistic hair or fused meshes rather than the separate ribbon-like cards used for stylized game characters and avatars. The prior stylized hair-card generator, CHARM, relies on long autoregressive control-point sequences.
method: Use a single image as input to generate a stylized, card-based hairstyle.
Represent the hairstyle as an unordered set of artist-defined hair-card primitives instead of a sequential list of control points.
Target separate card geometry suitable for spring-bone animation; the provided abstract does not detail the architecture or training procedure.
impact: HairDeck proposes a representation aligned with game and avatar production workflows, potentially reducing manual hair-card authoring. The supplied abstract does not report quantitative results or runtime comparisons.
visual_elements: Pipeline diagram: single character image → HairDeck → separated hair cards → animated hairstyle.
Representation comparison: CHARM’s ordered control-point sequence versus HairDeck’s unordered card set.
Exploded hairstyle view with each ribbon-like card shown in a different color.
Spring-bone illustration showing how individual hair cards bend during character motion.
paper_title: HairDeck: Animation-Ready Stylized Hair Cards from a Single Image
paper_authors: Yuze He, Yixiang Wei, Wang Zhao, Chuhao Chen, Yanning Zhou
